outputs.summary: Discovered an ARM64 cluster, installed the ARM Flux Operator, and ran the osu_latency benchmark 5 times. After several debugging iterations to fix the MiniCluster spec (incorrect flux container image and wrong number of tasks), all runs completed successfully. The key parameters were using 2 tasks on 2 nodes, leveraging the AWS EFA for low latency, and using an ARM-compatible container for Flux.

final_fom.reasons: The OSU Latency benchmark is a fundamental measure of point-to-point communication performance in high-performance computing. The test requires exactly two MPI processes, hence the `tasks` parameter was set to 2. The use of AWS Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) is crucial for achieving low latency, as it allows for OS-bypass networking, significantly reducing the overhead of communication protocols. One of the five runs (run 3) shows markedly lower latency for small messages (~7.5us vs ~13us), which is likely attributable to the Kubernetes scheduler placing both pods on the same physical node, resulting in much faster shared-memory communication rather than network communication. The other four runs show consistent inter-node latency. The variance in latency for very large message sizes (e.g., 1MB) can be attributed to buffer effects and network congestion.
